node.label: Fundamental Rights & Duties
node.summary: Articles 19, 21, 25, 48A, 51A(g) as they come up in court rulings and debates.

facts.text: Right to protest vs preventive detention (Jantar Mantar rally stopped at Minto Road): Art. 19(1)(a) and (b) guarantee speech and peaceful assembly, subject to reasonable restrictions under Art. 19(2) and 19(3).
facts.plain: Right to protest vs preventive detention (Jantar Mantar rally stopped at Minto Road): Art. 19(1)(a) and (b) guarantee speech and peaceful assembly, subject to reasonable restrictions under Art. 19(2) and 19(3).

facts.text: Op-ed view: celebration is not an 'automatic licence' to expose others to health risks. Regulate with standards and accountability rather than choose between a blanket ban and a free-for-all.
facts.plain: Op-ed view: celebration is not an 'automatic licence' to expose others to health risks. Regulate with standards and accountability rather than choose between a blanket ban and a free-for-all.

facts.text: **Art. 48A** (Directive Principle) asks the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife; **Art. 51A(g)** makes protecting the environment a Fundamental Duty.
facts.plain: Art. 48A (Directive Principle) asks the State to protect the environment, forests and wildlife; Art. 51A(g) makes protecting the environment a Fundamental Duty.

facts.text: The SC called cracker-bursting a religious practice for Deepavali but held that **Art. 25(1)** is a 'qualified' right, subject to public order, morality and health, and must be read with **Art. 21** (right to a healthy environment).
facts.plain: The SC called cracker-bursting a religious practice for Deepavali but held that Art. 25(1) is a 'qualified' right, subject to public order, morality and health, and must be read with Art. 21 (right to a healthy environment).

facts.text: SC judge **Justice Ujjal Bhuyan** said **scientific temper**, a Fundamental Duty under **Article 51A(h)**, must reach students' capacity to think rationally; a society that fears questions becomes vulnerable to misinformation and authoritarianism.
facts.plain: SC judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said scientific temper, a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(h), must reach students' capacity to think rationally; a society that fears questions becomes vulnerable to misinformation and authoritarianism.

facts.text: Precedent: in **Anuj Garg v. Hotel Association of India (2008)**, the SC struck down a Punjab Excise Act ban on employing women in bars, rejecting 'protective' discrimination.
facts.plain: Precedent: in Anuj Garg v. Hotel Association of India (2008), the SC struck down a Punjab Excise Act ban on employing women in bars, rejecting 'protective' discrimination.

facts.text: Kerala HC (Justice **P. Gopinath**) struck down the rule in the **Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002** that barred women from working in **toddy shops**, as violating equality, the right to livelihood and non-discrimination.
facts.plain: Kerala HC (Justice P. Gopinath) struck down the rule in the Kerala Abkari Shops Disposal Rules, 2002 that barred women from working in toddy shops, as violating equality, the right to livelihood and non-discrimination.

facts.text: Bombay HC (Nagpur Bench) held the **2011** arrest of activist **Arun Ferreira** illegal, violating **Articles 21 and 22**, and ordered ₹2 lakh compensation. Ferreira is also an accused in the **2018 Bhima Koregaon** case.
facts.plain: Bombay HC (Nagpur Bench) held the 2011 arrest of activist Arun Ferreira illegal, violating Articles 21 and 22, and ordered ₹2 lakh compensation. Ferreira is also an accused in the 2018 Bhima Koregaon case.

facts.text: **NALSA v. Union of India (2014)** recognised transgender persons as a '**third gender**'; Parliament later passed the **Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019**.
facts.plain: NALSA v. Union of India (2014) recognised transgender persons as a 'third gender'; Parliament later passed the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.

facts.text: A PIL by the India chapter of **Women's Declaration International** challenges the regime built on the **NALSA judgment (2014)** that recognised transgender identity, saying sex-marker changes in documents dilute women's rights; a CJI Surya Kant Bench issued notice.
facts.plain: A PIL by the India chapter of Women's Declaration International challenges the regime built on the NALSA judgment (2014) that recognised transgender identity, saying sex-marker changes in documents dilute women's rights; a CJI Surya Kant Bench issued notice.

facts.text: **Jantar Mantar** was denotified as a protest site on **11 Oct**; the INDIA bloc's 1 Nov 'Chalo Dilli' rally at **Ramlila Maidan** was its first big protest since, with 3,000+ police and AI-enabled CCTV.
